scene.note: The day book is built one file at a time into object files, linked into one program, and reads the day into a class that sums it up.

value.label: goes in
values: a stream of the day's lines, a heading first

steps.note: The day's file arrives as a stream, for the day book to fill itself from.
The heading and blank lines are skipped, and every good line becomes a repair in the book.
The book holds the day, and says how many lines it could not take.
Kasimir asks which repair of the day took longest.
The library's algorithm walks the repairs with a rule that compares their minutes.

value.label: comes out
values: where that repair is in the book, or nowhere

steps.note: The answer points at the repair inside the book, or at nothing when the day was empty.
The summary is declared once in a header, and any file that includes it can ask for it.
The book is only read: how many, how long, and which took longest.
Three lines reach the bench, through whatever stream was handed over.
Each .cpp file of the program gets a line of its own in the script.

value.label: one per file
values: a compiled file, with its flags

steps.note: Each file is compiled apart into an object file, with the warnings turned up.
One last step joins every object file into the program Kasimir runs.
